topic.title: Graph-Aware Attention and Language Models
topic.overview: Graph representations encode relationships that ordinary token order may obscure. This topic studies how attention models can preserve topology, structural similarity, and multi-hop connections while retaining flexible long-range computation. Methods combine graph encoders with Transformers or incorporate graph structure directly into attention and positional geometry.
topic.whyItMatters: A sequence representation of a graph can lose important relationships or introduce arbitrary ordering effects. Structural information must influence actual computation, not merely appear as a decorative positional feature.
topic.evolution: Early representatives connect neural architectures to graph kernels and transferable relational structures. Later graph Transformers use rooted subgraph representations and integrate textual nodes. Recent language-model approaches encode graph distance alongside token position and adjust structural attention inside decoder-only models, seeking reasoning that respects both graph connectivity and causal generation order.
openQuestions: How can attention distinguish meaningful structural differences from graph symmetries?
Which graph encodings generalize to unseen topologies without task-specific retraining?

papers.tldr: GIT uses task-trees to unify graph prediction tasks and learn transferable knowledge through reconstruction-based pretraining.

papers.title: Vision Graph Prompting via Semantic Low-Rank Decomposition
papers.tldr: Vision Graph Prompting uses low-rank semantic structure to adapt vision graph models efficiently, reaching performance comparable to full fine-tuning in experiments.

papers.title: A Closer Look at Graph Transformers: Cross-Aggregation and Beyond
papers.tldr: UGCFormer uses interactions between graph structure and node attributes to build an efficient graph transformer with linear computational complexity.

papers.title: Defining and Discovering Hyper-meta-paths for Heterogeneous Hypergraphs
papers.tldr: HHNN learns useful compositions of hypergraph relationships to improve both prediction performance and interpretability.

papers.title: Dynamic Bundling with Large Language Models for Zero-Shot Inference on Text-Attributed Graphs
papers.tldr: DENSE uses language-model labels for bundles of node texts to train graph neural networks, refining the bundles to reduce noise.

papers.title: FoGE: Fock Space inspired encoding for graph prompting
papers.tldr: FoGE uses a parameter-free graph encoder inspired by Fock space to support graph question answering with a frozen language model.

papers.title: From Sequence to Structure: Uncovering Substructure Reasoning in Transformers
papers.tldr: The paper develops and tests an account of how Transformer layers identify graph substructures from sequential inputs.

papers.title: Generalizable Insights for Graph Transformers in Theory and Practice
papers.tldr: The Generalized-Distance Transformer connects expressivity analysis with broad experiments to identify graph Transformer design choices that transfer across applications.

papers.title: Generative Graph Pattern Machine
papers.tldr: Generative Graph Pattern Machine learns from sequences of graph substructures and shows improved scaling and transfer across graph tasks.

papers.title: Graph Your Own Prompt
papers.tldr: Graph Consistency Regularization aligns feature relationships with class-aware prediction graphs to improve representation structure and generalization.

papers.title: GraphChain: Large Language Models for Large-scale Graph Analysis via Tool Chaining
papers.tldr: GraphChain learns tool sequences that compress graph information and adapts a frozen language-model policy to different graph structures.

papers.title: GraphMaster: Automated Graph Synthesis via LLM Agents in Data-Limited Environments
papers.tldr: GraphMaster coordinates four language-model agents to synthesize semantically coherent, structurally consistent graph data from limited examples.

papers.title: GraphTOP: Graph Topology-Oriented Prompting for Graph Neural Networks
papers.tldr: GraphTOP adapts frozen graph neural networks by learning sparse local edge rewiring, outperforming six baselines in reported node-classification experiments.

papers.title: HubGT: Fast Graph Transformer with Decoupled Hierarchy Labeling
papers.tldr: HubGT precomputes a hub-label hierarchy to remove graph processing from training and scale graph transformers efficiently.

papers.title: On Logic-based Self-Explainable Graph Neural Networks
papers.tldr: LogiX-GIN embeds logic layers in a graph neural network so its predictions come with rules aligned with its internal computations.

papers.title: One Prompt Fits All: Universal Graph Adaptation for Pretrained Models
papers.tldr: UniPrompt uses a theoretical analysis of graph prompts to guide adaptation across pretrained models and downstream domains while preserving the input graph.

papers.title: OPTFM: A Scalable Multi-View Graph Transformer for Hierarchical Pre-Training in Combinatorial Optimization
papers.tldr: OPTFM learns reusable graph embeddings with linear-time attention and dual-level pretraining, outperforming task-specific approaches across tested optimization tasks.

papers.title: Relieving the Over-Aggregating Effect in Graph Transformers
papers.tldr: Wideformer splits graph attention aggregation into parallel processes and prioritizes their outputs to reduce dilution of important messages.

papers.title: Restricted Global-Aware Graph Filters Bridging GNNs and Transformer for Node Classification
papers.tldr: Recasting graph-transformer components as constrained spectral filters improves generalization by controlling test-error oscillations.

papers.title: Rethinking Tokenized Graph Transformers for Node Classification
papers.tldr: SwapGT improves node classification through semantically informed token swapping and alignment of representations learned from multiple token sequences.

papers.title: SSTAG: Structure-Aware Self-Supervised Learning Method for Text-Attributed Graphs
papers.tldr: SSTAG distills language and graph knowledge into scalable models and uses memory anchors to improve transfer across text-attributed graphs.

papers.title: $\texttt{G1}$: Teaching LLMs to Reason on Graphs with Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: G1 uses reinforcement learning on synthetic graph tasks to improve graph reasoning and transfer to unseen tasks and encodings.

papers.title: The quest for the GRAph Level autoEncoder (GRALE)
papers.tldr: GRALE encodes and reconstructs variable-sized graphs with jointly learned differentiable matching.

papers.title: Unifying and Enhancing Graph Transformers via a Hierarchical Mask Framework
papers.tldr: M³Dphormer combines complementary attention masks and adaptive computation to improve graph Transformer performance.

papers.title: UniGTE: Unified Graph–Text Encoding for Zero-Shot Generalization across Graph Tasks and Domains
papers.tldr: UniGTE combines structure-aware graph–text encoding with a frozen language decoder to achieve strong zero-shot transfer across graph tasks and domains.

papers.title: Adaptive Recurrent Message Passing for Test Time Computing on Graphs
papers.tldr: AdaR uses step-aware recurrent graph updates to adapt test-time computation without changing model parameters.

papers.title: Beyond Tokens: Enhancing RTL Quality Estimation via Structural Graph Learning
papers.tldr: StructRTL improves early hardware quality estimates by learning circuit structure and distilling knowledge from post-mapping netlists.

papers.title: DANCE: Dynamic, Available, Neighbor-gated Condensation for Federated Text-Attributed Graphs
papers.tldr: DANCE refreshes graph condensation during federated training and preserves source evidence, improving reported accuracy while reducing token use.

papers.title: DiP-G: Discrete Prompting for Graph Neural Networks
papers.tldr: DiP-G learns discrete graph prompts directly, addressing the mismatch caused by training with continuous edges and discretizing them for inference.

papers.title: Enhancing LLMs for Graph Tasks via Graph-aware LoRA Generation
papers.tldr: GaRA generates graph-conditioned LoRA weight updates to inject whole-graph information into language models for zero-shot graph tasks.

papers.title: ERAlign: Energy-based Representation Alignment of GNNs and LLMs on Text-attributed Graphs
papers.tldr: ERAlign uses energy-based training to align graph and text representation distributions for learning on text-attributed graphs.

papers.title: Feature-Aware (Hyper)graph Generation via Next-Scale Prediction
papers.tldr: FAHNES jointly generates connections and features across scales, supporting large featured graphs and hypergraphs with strong reported performance.

papers.title: GFMate: Empowering Graph Foundation Models with Test-time Prompt Tuning
papers.tldr: GFMate improves graph foundation models with prompts applied after pretraining and tuned using labeled and unlabeled target-domain data.

papers.title: GP2F: Cross-Domain Graph Prompting with Adaptive Fusion of Pre-trained Graph Neural Networks
papers.tldr: GP2F adaptively combines frozen pretrained graph knowledge with lightweight task adaptation to improve cross-domain few-shot classification.

papers.title: Graph Alignment for Benchmarking Graph Neural Networks and Learning Positional Encodings
papers.tldr: Graph alignment provides adjustable-difficulty GNN benchmarks and pretraining that yields useful structural node representations.

papers.title: Graph is a Substrate Across Data Modalities
papers.tldr: G-Substrate uses a shared graph schema and varied training roles to accumulate reusable structure across modalities and tasks.

papers.title: GraphPFN: A Prior-Data Fitted Graph Foundation Model
papers.tldr: GraphPFN combines graph-specific architecture and synthetic graph pretraining to achieve strong node-level results across real-world datasets.

papers.title: Message Tuning Outshines Graph Prompt Tuning: A Prismatic Space Perspective
papers.tldr: Message tuning adapts frozen graph networks with learnable message prototypes whose capacity can exceed graph prompt tuning’s theoretical bound.

papers.title: MIMO-LP: A Multi-Input Multi-Output Framework for Subgraph-based Link Prediction
papers.tldr: MIMO-LP shares message passing across multiple link queries, reporting 14–44-fold speedups with comparable predictive performance.

papers.title: Multi-scale Explainer for Graph Neural Networks
papers.tldr: MSExplainer learns consistent graph explanations at multiple scales, generally improving fidelity while preserving the complexity order of single-scale methods.

papers.title: Plain Transformers are Surprisingly Powerful Link Predictors
papers.tldr: PENCIL shows that a plain Transformer attending to sampled local subgraphs can deliver strong, parameter-efficient link prediction.

papers.title: Rotary Position Encodings for Graphs
papers.tldr: WIRE adapts rotary position encodings to graph structure using Laplacian-based rotations while remaining compatible with linear attention.

papers.title: SLASH the Sink: Sharpening Structural Attention Inside LLMs
papers.tldr: SLASH redistributes attention without training to strengthen graph-structure signals already present inside language models.

papers.title: View Space: Learning Representation across Arbitrary Graphs
papers.tldr: Recurrent GVT uses graph-induced view-space representations to transfer a pretrained node-classification model across datasets with different feature spaces.

papers.title: Weaving Graph over Tokens: Contextualizing Structured Sequences for LLMs
papers.tldr: Weaver embeds graph distances into decoder attention to support graph reasoning directly within a generative language model.
